gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/initial recommended=1

Case G - pending contract proposal

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/contract-exception recommended=1

Current wording: The build version is served at /health.
Proposed wording: The build version is served at /status.

Today the spec requires the build version to be served at the existing health address. Moving it to the new status address gains nothing for serving the build version, because the existing health address can already return it, and it changes where callers must look. I recommend preserve contract because a repair under the current requirement delivers the same result.

Pick one:
1. preserve contract - keep the current requirement, drop this proposal, and continue repairing the PR so the health address serves the build version. [recommended]
2. accept contract change - amend the spec to require the status address, then continue delivery against the new wording.
3. stop - remove the worktree if it is clean and pushed, and leave the PR as it is.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: The After wording moved `contract` as intended, and it moved `authority` too, because that fact requires the three contract sentences in Case G. Case G now shows a Current/Proposed wording pair that keeps /health and /status, followed by exactly three path-free sentences directly above Pick one. Those cover the current requirement, what moving the address gains or costs, and that the existing address can already return the build version. Before had only a proposal sentence and a one-line reason, both containing endpoint paths. No fact that Before kept was lost. Three places are close to the line and worth pinning down in the wording. In Case G the "can already serve it" explanation sits in the second sentence, and the third only says a repair "delivers the same result"; assigning one job per sentence would stop that drifting. In Case B the deliver row now says "retry the merge"; it passes only because the condition "only after another reviewer approves" comes first, so require the condition to lead, or it reads as a merge promise. The A-F reports now cite APP-91, which no fact forbids there, but the Change bars tracker IDs from the contract explanation, so say explicitly that IDs must stay out of the Case G sentences and the recommendation reasons.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: The only fact that moved is contract, and it moved as intended. Before's Case G had no current/proposed wording pair and put /health in both the explanation and the recommendation sentence. After shows the pair with /health and /status, then gives three path-free sentences directly above Pick one, with preserve contract first and no report. The pass is thin on one point: the second sentence says the proposal "changes the required address" but leaves the reader to infer what that costs or gains. Make that explicit, for example by saying that changing the address gains nothing the current one cannot already provide and would move a requirement callers rely on, and keep the third sentence on why the existing address can already serve the build version. Cases A-F kept every fact; the new "You cannot approve your own PR" line, the tighter gate-line spacing and the "Description correction: old -> new" preview did no harm. To keep it that way, keep the recommendation reason as the last line before Pick one, keep the Case B deliver row conditioned on another reviewer approving, keep the Case C reason tied to the unchanged workflow approval, and do not let the Case G wording-pair labels spread into field-style lines in the other cases.
